producer.what: vqsv.game.ProbeWebBattleMath
producer.note: Calls the Java battle engines' own functions over fixed input grids and records what they returned. golden-battle-ai.json is the same probe applied to the decision path instead of the arithmetic: one row per enemy decision point of the production 1v1 turn, carrying the scripted public memory, the source-v1 answer, the observation the utility pass actually saw, the ranked candidates with their score breakdown, the shadow-boundary invariant and the decision the canary adapter committed. The Web port reimplements the rules and is graded against these rows; a row is never copied into TypeScript arithmetic, and these tables carry answers only.

producer.what: vqsv.game.ExportWebDataCatalogs
producer.note: The one home for a Pet species: identity, metadata, the quality the source row authors, the stat-growth path the engine actually reads, that path's numbers, and the ancestors whose stats floor them. Covers every id the engine can resolve, including boss, evolution, mutation and V4 forms, so no species data is read from a golden table. The anchors a record class kept as private constants are exported as growth tables too, replayed against the engine over every level and quality before the bake.

producer.what: vqsv.game.ExportWebDataCatalogs
producer.note: How long the win panel holds a level-up, how far the experience bar moves per tick, and how long it rests after reaching its target. The runtime keeps these as literals inside tickWinExpLevelUp, where reflection has nothing to read, so the harness takes them out of that method's own source and refuses the dump unless each pattern matches exactly once there. The Web guard re-reads the same method and refuses these bytes if a number moves.

producer.what: vqsv.game.ExportWebDataCatalogs
producer.note: The enemy decision catalog, printed as the Java decision path reads it rather than as the nine TSVs behind it: each encounter's authored policy row, its roster, items and phase list, the persona-plus-phase projection the utility pass consumes, the source lock that maps a runtime descriptor to the encounter identity, the B1 activation review that gates a Leader/Boss canary, and the weights BattleAiUtilityWeights.forProfile returns for each intelligence profile. The Web port reimplements scoring and selection and is graded against the golden decision rows; this file is the input those rules resolve, so no weight, bias set or modifier is restated in TypeScript.

producer.what: the buff/debuff rules the web build adds or changes on top of the Java-baked status tables; each rule follows its status description
VqsvBattleAnimationTables effect.mid/speffect.mid rows, P7 actor-effect mapping and SpriteAnimator frame timing
producer.note: Exports all seven columns of every source skill chunk plus every special-effect row, and bloodRow 0/1 (the per-tick float of the damage text and of the miss or status-name text). Actor sprite ids and frame durations are resolved through the same Java owners used by P7; the Web runtime contains no per-skill sprite table.

producer.what: vqsv.game.ExportWebDataCatalogs
producer.note: Each file is one table the engine has already resolved, so a Web number can be traced to the Java code path that produced it. The damage inputs are skill-rows (what each skill id resolves to after the three competing skill sources, plus which damage branch that id takes), element-chart (the element pairs the engine's own relation check answers true for), debuff-producers (which skill can put which status on a target, with what chance) and pet-level plus cau-vong-pet-level (the two ceilings an encounter level is clamped to). The status inputs are statuses (the identity, kind and lifetime policy of every status the engine can hold) and status-mechanics (how strong each buff is, the value each buff actually writes onto the unit when it is applied, which skill overrides that strength, which route a finished skill takes to apply a status, and which statuses the round-start pass shows an effect for). The written values are the one table here that the engine does not hand over: it computes them in a switch of its own, so they are declared in the harness and then replayed against that switch over a species by level grid before the bake is allowed to write the file, and a row the grid could not have caught fails the bake instead of shipping.

producer.what: the user's balance workbooks, layered over the Java catalog dumps in the data domain
producer.note: Deliberately not under data/: pack-provenance.mjs gives the data-java-harness bake owns() over that whole root, so a hand-authored file there would read as a stale Java output. A table here states which Java row it overrides and the guard test proves every field it does not.
